title: finding(release): no GitHub release or git tag has been created since 17.5.0 — Changesets CLI v3 stopped printing the `New tag:` lines `changesets/action@v1` parses, so 17.6.0 and 17.7.0 reached npm with no tag and no release
body:
## What is missing

The GitHub Releases page for this repository stops at the 17.5.0 set, created on 2026-08-14. Both later versions are on npm:

| version | npm | git tag `@object-ui/core@…` | GitHub releases |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 17.5.0 | 2026-08-14 | ✅ | ✅ one per package |
| 17.6.0 | 2026-08-24 | ❌ | ❌ |
| 17.7.0 | 2026-10-04 03:55Z | ❌ | ❌ |

The 17.7.0 publish run (37175007951) reports success in every step, including "Verify the release reached npm". All 39 published packages serve 17.7.0.

## Why

- `changeset-release.yml` publishes through `changesets/action@v1` (`publish: pnpm changeset:publish`). v1 learns what was published by **parsing the publish script's stdout** for `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` lines. Only for the packages it finds does it push the tag (`git.pushTag`) and create the GitHub release.
- objectui#5296 moved the repository to `@changesets/cli` v3 between the two releases. At the 17.5.0 tag, `package.json` declares `^2.31.1`. At the 17.6.0 release commit `59f61cfb` it declares `^3.0.0`, and the lockfile resolves `3.0.1`.
- CLI v3's `changeset publish` prints through `@clack/prompts` and reports published packages through an output report (`CHANGESETS_OUTPUT`). Its dist contains no `New tag` string: 0 occurrences in `@changesets/cli@3.0.1/dist`.
- v1 therefore sees zero published packages, pushes no tag and creates no release. Nothing fails: the npm verification step checks npm only. The workflow's own header notes this risk for v2 (#678: tags and releases "fail QUIETLY"). The CLI v3 bump triggered it under v1.

## How objectstack does it (port this)

`../objectstack` uses the same CLI v3 and still gets releases (17.6.0 has them):

- `scripts/release-publish.sh` runs `changeset publish` (which creates the tags locally), then ONE atomic `git push origin --tags`. objectstack#2191 explains why this is atomic: per-tag pushes raced GitHub's ref backend.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` step "Create GitHub Releases (bodies truncated to the API limit)" runs `node scripts/release-github-releases.mjs` with `RELEASE_VERSION`. The script creates one release per public package from its CHANGELOG entry. It is idempotent, and it truncates bodies to the API limit with a self-test battery.

## Fix

1. In the publish lane, after `changesets/action@v1` publishes, push the tags `changeset publish` created on the runner and create one GitHub release per published package for the version the lane published (`needs.lane.outputs.manifest_version`). Port `release-github-releases.mjs` and its self-tests, adapted to this workspace's package enumeration, rather than re-deriving it. The step must run only on the publish lane (`push` with the version not on npm before), never on `schedule` / `workflow_dispatch`.
2. Keep `changesets/action@v1`. The pin's reasoning in the workflow header is unchanged. Do not set `createGithubReleases: false` unless the new step fully replaces it.
3. Backfill, after the fix lands: put each tag on the commit its version was **published from**, which is not always the version commit, and create releases for both versions with the ported script.
   - **17.6.0:** published by run 32739909630 from `b65fe911de`. Its "Publish to npm" step ran 14:41:58–14:45:08Z on 2026-08-24. The version commit `59f61cfb` (#4655) merged on 08-20, but objectui#5442's npm-keyed retry published 17.6.0 four days later from that later head.
   - **17.7.0:** published by run 37175007951 from `b493919c`, the #5400 merge.
